short: Recording a transaction in the period it actually happened in.
seoTitle: Cut-Off in Accounting — Meaning and Example
metaDescription: Cut-off is the rule that a transaction belongs to the period it happened in, not the period the paperwork arrived. Why cut-off errors distort two months.
definition: Cut-off is the rule that a transaction is recorded in the period in which it actually occurred, not the period in which the paperwork arrived or the money moved.
bodyHtml:
Why cut-off errors matter

Cut-off errors are the most common reason two consecutive months look strange. A March supplier bill posted in April makes March look profitable and April look bad, while the year total is unchanged. Anyone comparing months is then comparing noise.

How to get cut-off right

Under accrual accounting the test is when goods were received or the service was performed — evidenced by the goods receipt note or delivery date, not the invoice date or the payment date. At each month-end close, list the bills you expect but have not received and accrue for them rather than letting them slide into next month.

faq.question: What is a cut-off error?
faq.answer: Recording a transaction in the wrong period — typically a purchase bill posted when it arrived rather than when the goods were received.

faq.question: Does cut-off matter on cash basis?
faq.answer: Much less, because cash-basis books follow the payment date by design. It matters most under accrual accounting.
